body: AI Agents & MCPs & AI Workflow Automation • (~400 MCP servers for AI agents) • AI Automation / AI Agent with MCPs • AI Workflows & AI Agents • MCPs for AI Agents
plain_description: Activepieces is an open-source replacement for Zapier that lets you automate workflows and build AI agents without writing code. The big picture: connect 200+ apps through a visual drag-and-drop builder, with built-in AI capabilities and human-in-the-loop approvals. Here's why it matters: non-technical team members can create powerful automations, while developers can extend everything with custom TypeScript integrations.
technical_description: Activepieces is an open-source automation platform written in TypeScript that provides a visual workflow builder for creating AI-powered automations and integrations. It uses a pieces framework where each integration is an npm package, supporting hot reloading for local development. The platform exposes 280+ integrations as MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for use with LLM clients. It supports self-hosted deployment via Docker or Kubernetes (Helm), with enterprise features including SCIM, audit logs, and RBAC. Native AI pieces support multiple providers, and the platform includes human-in-the-loop approval steps, chat interfaces, and form inputs. Flows are fully versioned with support for loops, branches, auto-retries, and custom code with NPM.
title: Activepieces

body: Build Agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, with rich AI model and tool support on one collaborative workspace. Deploy on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted, so teams move from prototype to production without rebuilding the stack.
plain_description: The big picture: Dify lets you build AI-powered applications — chatbots, agents, and workflows — without writing code from scratch. Here's why it matters: you get a visual canvas to design AI workflows, connect to hundreds of LLMs, and add RAG pipelines, all in one collaborative workspace. The bottom line: teams can prototype and ship production AI apps faster, whether on cloud or self-hosted.
technical_description: Dify is an open-source LLM application development platform that provides a visual workflow builder, RAG pipeline, agent capabilities, and model management. The platform supports integration with hundreds of proprietary and open-source LLMs via inference providers and OpenAI API-compatible endpoints. It offers a prompt IDE, built-in tools for AI agents, LLMOps observability, and a Backend-as-a-Service API layer. Deployment is via Docker Compose with optional Kubernetes support through community Helm charts.
title: Dify

plain_description: Flowise lets anyone build AI agents and chatbots without writing code. Drag and drop components to connect language models, data sources, and business tools into automated workflows. Launch production-ready AI assistants in minutes on your own infrastructure or through the cloud.
technical_description: Flowise is an open-source, low-code platform for building LLM applications and AI agents through a visual node-based editor. It consists of a Node.js/Express server exposing REST APIs with auto-generated Swagger documentation, and a React frontend. The modular component architecture integrates with 100+ LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.), vector databases (Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate), document loaders, and agent frameworks. The server provides chat message handling, document storage, vector search, execution monitoring, and enterprise features. Deployment options include Docker, npm, and managed cloud hosting.
title: Flowise

body: Event Driven Orchestration & Scheduling Platform for Mission Critical Applications
plain_description: Kestra unifies data, AI, and infrastructure workflows into a single event-driven platform. Build reliable pipelines visually or in YAML, schedule them, and react to real-time events — all from one intuitive interface. The bottom line: replace brittle scripts and cron jobs with workflows you can see, manage, and scale.
technical_description: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration platform for data, AI, and infrastructure workflows. It uses a declarative YAML DSL to define directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflows composed of modular tasks with built-in scheduling, event triggers, error handling, retry policies, and subflow composition. The platform is implemented in Java on the JVM using the Micronaut framework and exposes a REST API alongside a web-based UI for workflow authoring, topology visualization, execution monitoring, and debugging. It supports multiple deployment topologies — standalone, worker-executor, and Kubernetes-native — with persistent backends for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and H2, and extends capabilities through a plugin ecosystem covering cloud services, databases, messaging systems, and scripting languages.
title: Kestra

body: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities. Combine visual building with custom code, self-host or cloud, 400+ integrations.
plain_description: Automate complex workflows and deploy AI agents without writing everything from scratch. n8n's visual canvas connects 1500+ apps and AI models so you can build automations that your business can trust. Deploy self-hosted or in the cloud and go from prototype to production fast.
technical_description: n8n is a fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI agent capabilities built in TypeScript on Node.js. It provides a visual node-based editor for constructing multi-step workflows that integrate JavaScript, Python, and 1500+ external services through a modular node system. The platform supports self-hosted deployment via Docker or npm and a managed cloud offering. Key capabilities include AI agent orchestration with support for multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, open-source models via Ollama), RAG pipelines with vector stores, document processing, MCP client/server integration, and enterprise features including RBAC, audit trails, source control, and log streaming.
title: n8n

body: Open-source developer platform to power your entire infra and turn scripts into webhooks, workflows and UIs. Fastest workflow engine (13x vs Airflow). Open-source alternative to Retool and Temporal.
plain_description: Windmill lets your engineering team turn scripts into internal tools, APIs, and automated workflows without needing a separate frontend team or multiple platforms. It replaces Retool-like UI builders and Temporal-like workflow engines with a single self-hosted solution. The bottom line: ship internal apps and automations in hours, not weeks.
technical_description: Windmill is an open-source developer platform implemented in Rust with a Svelte 5 frontend. It executes scripts written in Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash, SQL, GraphQL, PowerShell, Rust, Java, C#, and PHP, exposing them as auto-generated UIs, REST API endpoints, webhooks, scheduled jobs, or chained multi-step workflows. The platform uses a PostgreSQL-backed job queue with stateless API servers and workers, with sandboxed script execution via nsjail and PID namespace isolation. It supports triggers from Kafka, WebSockets, email, HTTP, and message queues, and integrates with OAuth/SSO providers including Google Workspace and Microsoft Azure. Deployment options include Docker Compose and Kubernetes Helm charts, with support for major cloud providers.
title: Windmill
